patch.value: Cross-process reproducibility gate: prove CLI and MCP deterministic runs are byte-identical and fail on ambient time leaks

Add a permanent release/CI acceptance gate that executes real CLI and MCP process workflows twice in isolated fresh workspaces with the same declared clock, tick, and seed, compares authoritative tracker and history bytes, and includes negative controls for invalid configuration and default-path variability.

The gate runs real packaged CLI and MCP transports rather than calling the context primitive directly; two isolated same-configuration runs compare byte-identical authoritative item and history outputs; a negative control proves differing seeds or absent process configuration is observable; invalid and partial environment contracts are covered; the gate is invoked by an existing mandatory CI path and has focused unit coverage
Turn process-level reproducibility from documentation into a mechanical release invariant
A future transport or timestamp call-site regression fails locally and in hosted CI with a replayable configuration
GH-1089 proves SDK-only tests can stay green while the shipped binary remains nondeterministic

value.text: A deterministic one-shot CLI process restarts its entropy sequence, so multi-step shell workflows need stable step-derived seeds. A serialized long-lived MCP transport should instead retain one validated process runner so its sequence advances across requests. Exercise both process lifetimes with authoritative byte comparisons; calling only the context primitive cannot prove the bundled transport boundary.
